data.summary: The plan front‑loads the student’s weak units (3 and 5) with focused study and live‑class support, then moves through the remaining curriculum while keeping a steady pace of 6 hours per week. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed full‑exam practice to consolidate knowledge and build test stamina.

weeks.focus: Introduce composite and implicit differentiation (Unit 3) and review basic limits.
tasks: Watch a tutorial on the Chain Rule and Implicit Differentiation (30 min).
Do 8 practice problems on applying the Chain Rule; check answers with solution guide (45 min).
Do 6 implicit differentiation problems; verify each step (45 min).
Review limit definitions; complete 5 limit‑evaluation exercises from the textbook (30 min).
Summarize key differences between average and instantaneous rate of change in a one‑page note (30 min).
Create a quick‑reference sheet for limit properties and chain‑rule formulas (30 min).

weeks.focus: Live class on Unit 3; solidify chain rule and implicit differentiation.
tasks: Attend live class 10600 (90 min).
Redo the class’s example problems without notes (45 min).
Complete 10 additional FRQs on chain rule and implicit differentiation; grade with scoring guide (60 min).
Watch a short video on differentiating inverse functions (3.3) (20 min).
Do 5 practice problems on inverse function differentiation (30 min).
Reflect: write 3 bullet points on common mistakes in implicit differentiation (15 min).

weeks.focus: Begin Analytical Applications of Differentiation (Unit 5) – Mean Value & Extreme Value Theorems.
tasks: Read textbook sections on Mean Value Theorem and Extreme Value Theorem (45 min).
Do 8 problems applying MVT; verify with answer key (45 min).
Do 8 problems locating global vs. local extrema; label critical points (45 min).
Create a two‑column chart comparing hypotheses and conclusions of MVT and EVT (30 min).
Complete a short quiz on identifying critical points (20 min).
Review notes and correct any errors (25 min).

weeks.focus: Continue Unit 5 – First Derivative Test and increasing/decreasing intervals.
tasks: Watch a video on the First Derivative Test (20 min).
Solve 10 problems determining intervals of increase/decrease (45 min).
Solve 10 problems using the First Derivative Test to locate relative extrema (45 min).
Create a summary sheet of steps for the First Derivative Test (30 min).
Do a mixed set of 6 FRQs covering 5.1‑5.4; grade with rubric (60 min).
Review errors and rewrite correct solutions (40 min).

weeks.focus: Live class review of Unit 5; reinforce earlier topics and finish First Derivative Test.
tasks: Attend live class 10601 (90 min).
Redo class examples without notes (45 min).
Complete 6 additional FRQs on extrema and critical points (60 min).
Finish any remaining 5.4 First Derivative Test problems not covered in class (30 min).
Update the summary sheet to include class insights (20 min).
Quick self‑quiz: identify which theorem applies to each of 8 scenarios (35 min).

weeks.focus: Contextual Applications of Differentiation (Unit 4) – motion and related rates.
tasks: Read sections on interpreting derivatives in context and related rates (40 min).
Solve 6 straight‑line motion problems (position, velocity, acceleration) (45 min).
Solve 6 related‑rates problems from past FRQs (60 min).
Create a flowchart for setting up related‑rates equations (30 min).
Do a mixed set of 8 FRQs covering 4.1‑4.4; grade with scoring guide (60 min).
Review and correct any mistakes (45 min).

weeks.focus: Integration fundamentals and introduction to differential equations (Units 6 & 7).
tasks: Watch a video on definite integrals and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (30 min).
Complete 8 problems evaluating definite integrals using FTC (45 min).
Read about modeling with differential equations; do 5 simple modeling problems (45 min).
Sketch slope fields for 3 given differential equations (30 min).
Do a short quiz on FTC concepts (20 min).
Summarize key steps for solving basic differential equations in a one‑page cheat sheet (30 min).

weeks.focus: Live class on Integration basics (Unit 6) – accumulations and Riemann sums.
tasks: Attend live class 10602 (90 min).
Redo class examples on accumulations and Riemann sums (45 min).
Complete 8 additional Riemann‑sum problems with different sample points (60 min).
Do 6 problems converting accumulation functions to integrals (30 min).
Update integration summary sheet with class notes (25 min).
Quick self‑check: estimate area under 4 new curves using left, right, and midpoint sums (30 min).

weeks.focus: Mixed review – Units 1‑4 FRQs and key concepts.
tasks: Do a timed set of 5 FRQs covering limits and continuity (30 min).
Do a timed set of 5 FRQs covering basic differentiation rules (30 min).
Review answers using scoring guide; note any recurring errors (45 min).
Complete 4 related‑rates FRQs for additional practice (45 min).
Create a one‑page “big ideas” map linking limits, derivatives, and applications (30 min).
Spend remaining time revisiting any weak problem types identified (30 min).

weeks.focus: Full‑exam timed practice and final review.
tasks: Take a full‑length AP Calculus AB practice exam under timed conditions (2 hrs).
Score the exam using the official rubric; record score breakdown (30 min).
Review every incorrect response; rewrite correct solution with explanation (1 hr).
Do a rapid‑review flashcard session covering all theorem statements (30 min).
Create a personalized “exam‑day checklist” (15 min).
Relaxation breathing exercise and mental‑prep routine (15 min).

data.final_week_advice: On exam day, follow your checklist, trust the preparation you’ve built, manage time wisely, and use your quick‑reference sheets only for last‑minute checks. Stay calm, read each question carefully, and apply the systematic problem‑solving steps you practiced throughout the plan.
